models.title: Sortino ratio
models.summary: Return above the minimum acceptable return per unit of target semi-standard deviation.

relationship.locator: PDF: LM1 Sortino Eqs 22-23 with Exhibit 16, printed pp. 53-54 (PDF pp. 61-62): (6.0%-4.0%)/3.07% = 0.65; Example 12 Q1, printed p. 54 (PDF p. 62): (0.10-0.03)/0.08 = 0.88
relationship.translation_notes: rp is mean portfolio return, rt the MAR/target, sd the target semi-standard deviation (computed by the sibling semivariance record, then square-rooted). Decimals.

assumptions: MAR fixed for the measurement; sd from downside-only deviations below the MAR.
limitations: Investor-specific MAR makes cross-sectional comparison difficult; not a risk premium (return above minimum, per PDF).

rejection_cases.reason: Downside deviation is structurally required; without it the ratio has no risk scale.
Guard sd > 0 violated; zero downside deviation makes the ratio undefined.

models.title: Target semivariance (downside)
models.summary: Mean of squared below-target deviations; family holds precomputed min(r_t - r_T, 0)^2 values.

relationship.original_equation: sigma_D^2 = sum min(r_t - r_T, 0)^2 / N (Eq24 without the 1/2 power)
relationship.locator: PDF: LM1 target semideviation Eq 24 with Exhibit 16, printed pp. 53-54 (PDF pp. 61-62): sum min2 = 0.0094, /10, sqrt = 3.07%; Example 12 Q5 solution, printed p. 56 (PDF p. 64): sum = 0.004, /4, sqrt = 3.16%
relationship.translation_notes: Family M holds precomputed squared shortfalls (squaring documented here as the per-element construction). Record outputs the semivariance; sigma_D = sqrt(output) per Eq24 (sqrt(0.00094) = 3.07%, sqrt(0.001) = 3.16%). Decimals.

assumptions: MAR fixed across the series; only below-target deviations enter (above-target contribute 0).
limitations: Grammar has no sqrt: the PDF's Eq24 standard deviation is the documented sqrt inverse. Annualization of multi-period inputs follows the source convention.

models.title: Upside capture ratio
models.summary: Manager return relative to benchmark return in up markets (benchmark return nonnegative).

relationship.translation_notes: Geometric-average-period returns in the PDF oracles; ratio in decimal (72.8% = 0.728). Above (below) 100% suggests outperformance (underperformance).

variables.definition: Manager return for the up-market span, decimal
Benchmark return for the same span, decimal

assumptions: Up-market span only (benchmark return nonnegative); opposite-sign returns yield negative ratios (informative, per PDF).
limitations: Geometric-average formulation in the source exhibits; single-period point ratios share the form but the oracles are span averages.
